item.title: ASEAN Outcomes and Trump’s Manila Visit
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump joined dozens of world leaders in Manila on November 17 and 18 during the annual ASEAN Summit and related meetings. What happened at the meetings, and how will they impact U.S.-China competition and U.S.–Southeast Asia relations moving forward?

item.title: Human Rights Initiative Director's Note: November 2026 Edition
item.description: The November 2026 edition of the Human Rights Initiative Director's Note where Andrew Friedman shares his reflections on human rights and democracy issues occupying significant space in his mind, highlights key HRI ongoings, and spotlights notable articles and videos he's come across.

item.title: Dealing with Canada
item.description: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch discusses how the new Congress might address tariffs on Canada.

item.title: Data Is Physical; Its Security Must Be, Too
item.description: Data centers are the invisible backbone of the internet. As they continue to expand, policymakers need to consider protecting the physical infrastructure that houses the functioning of daily life.

item.title: What AI Agent Attacks Mean for India’s Cyberspace
item.description: India has disclosed its first cyber incident carried out by an AI agent rather than a human. How New Delhi and Washington respond is an early test of whether they can manage frontier AI risk together.

item.title: What Do the Results of the Midterm Elections Mean for Clean Energy and Climate?
item.description: Democratic gains in Congress and several states will reshape U.S. energy politics but are unlikely to reverse federal climate rollbacks. Instead, affordability, data center costs, and state utility regulators are poised to define the next two years of clean energy policy.

The Nvidia Controversy Should Put Corporations on High Alert About Threats to U.S. National Security
item.description: Jensen Huang's resignation shows that for companies at the center of U.S.-China competition, protecting executives and planning for their sudden departure are now national security issues.
